clue.text: Another drink for artist, sort of

definitions.meaning: a drink taken straight after another, such as beer after whisky
a craftsman who engraves or embosses metal, a kind of artist

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the uncommon one: a chaser is a metal engraver, which the setter calls an artist of a sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a follow-up drink, and an engraver of metalwork.

clue.text: Point extended in rash manner

parts.note: a head is a point, as of a headland or spear
extended means long, drawn out

explanation.surface: Someone making a lengthy point is acting rashly.
explanation.definitionFit: To act headlong is to act impetuously, without thinking first.

clue.text: Becoming accomplished after case

indicators.note: after tells us the word for accomplished follows the word for case

parts.note: a suit is a case in law, a lawsuit
able means skilled, accomplished

explanation.surface: Someone grows accomplished after handling a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' is the adjective meaning fitting, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A becoming outfit is appropriate or fitting, a synonym.

clue.text: Terrier vet's almost mistaken for another dog

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be put in another order
almost means the short word is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: the possessive of vet supplies the word vet

explanation.surface: A vet confuses a terrier with a different breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims VET to VE; 'mistaken' then rearranges TERRIER plus VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gundog breed, so another dog after the terrier.

clue.text: Divine female in house any MP honours

indicators.note: in signals that the letters lie inside the run house any MP honours

explanation.surface: A goddess is among the honours an MP gives in the House.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea nymph is a minor goddess of the ocean in classical myth, such as a Nereid.

clue.text: Like modern materials, not amenable to analysis?

definitions.meaning: describing fabrics treated so they keep their size in the wash
playfully, resisting a psychiatrist, slang shrink, and their analysis

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'shrink' as slang for a psychiatrist: someone who resists the shrink will not undergo analysis.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated fabrics do not contract in the wash; the joke reading has a patient who resists a therapist.

clue.text: You are, I heard, dividing food to provide some

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the word for food apart by going into its middle

parts.note: nosh is informal British slang for food

indicators.note: heard tells us the words are said aloud and written as letters with the same sound

parts.note: spoken, these words sound like the letters U, R and I

explanation.surface: Someone splits their food so as to offer a share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points back to the food already mentioned, so the definition means to provide food.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed someone is to supply them with sustenance, a synonym.

clue.text: How like brothers to surround female swimmer

indicators.note: to surround means the word for brothers is wrapped round the letter for female

parts.note: monkish means like monks, brothers of a religious order

explanation.surface: Friars encircle a woman who is out swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: A monkfish is a sea fish, and in crosswords any fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Epicurean fellow involved in American crime

indicators.note: involved in means the word for fellow is set inside the crime

parts.note: heist is American slang for a robbery
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: A gourmet man is mixed up in a US robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epicurean' looks like an adjective describing the fellow, but it is the definition, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure devotes himself to pleasure, especially fine food: a pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: On abandoning containers at sea, find this one…

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
abandoning means the two letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Containers lost overboard: you will find one of them washed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops the two letters, leaving CTAINERS for 'at sea' to rearrange; the dots carry the shipwreck into the next clue, and 'this one' means one of those containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a metal container, one of the kind just named.

clue.text: …wrecked on the rocks

definitions.meaning: idiom for bankrupt or in serious trouble, as a failing business

explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots tie it to the previous clue's shipwreck picture, but the clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean destroyed or broke: a wrecked ship and a business heading for collapse.

clue.text: European tree seen by a lake

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps
banian is a variant spelling of banyan, the Indian fig tree

explanation.surface: A tree stands beside a lake in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Albania, a Balkan country, is a European.

clue.text: Light meal for pet at home

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff
in means at home

explanation.surface: A small snack is prepared for a pet indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal, but it means a sulk or petty quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light lunch.

clue.text: Irritable, as it happens — having temper, losing head

parts.note: live means broadcast in real time, as it happens

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word for temper is dropped

parts.note: Irish is an informal word for temper, as in getting one's Irish up

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross on the spot, their temper flaring until they lose their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts IRISH to RISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling liverish means feeling queasy and peevish, so grumpy.

clue.text: Station fleet to hold position

parts.note: a stand is a station or post
fleet means swift, fast

explanation.surface: Ships are ordered to keep their places at a naval station.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain firm without retreating is to keep one's ground.

clue.text: Ill-feeling for feuding Veronese family? Not half!

indicators.note: Not half means the front half of the family name is removed

parts.note: in Romeo and Juliet the Montagues of Verona feud with the Capulets

explanation.surface: Bad blood between the warring houses of Verona, emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' sounds like the British exclamation meaning very much, but it drops the first half, MONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ague is a feverish shivering illness, so literally a feeling of being ill.

clue.text: Seating for mad March 'are, we hear

indicators.note: mad means the letters of the month are thrown into disorder
we hear tells us the word is said aloud and written as another with the same sound

parts.note: hare with its h dropped, as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: A chair for the proverbial mad March hare, spoken in dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges MARCH to ARMCH; 'are, dropping the H of hare, sounds like AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair is a padded chair with arm supports, a piece of seating.

clue.text: Mounting disorder

explanation.definitionFit: A rising up of the sun or of a population: ascent and rebellion.

clue.text: Tiny particle with end replaced

indicators.note: end replaced means the final letter of with is shifted to another spot

explanation.surface: A minute speck has its tip put back.
explanation.walkthrough: The H at the end of WITH moves to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: A whit is the smallest amount, a jot.

clue.text: Partiality is a shortcoming

definitions.meaning: a fondness, as in a soft spot for chocolate

explanation.surface: Being biased is a failing.
explanation.definitionFit: A liking one cannot resist, and a fault or defect.

clue.text: Not busy during later part of play, sweetheart

parts.note: in means during
Act IV is a late act of a five-act play
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A sweetheart idles through the closing scenes of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' reads as a lover, but it means the heart of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means idle, doing nothing.

clue.text: Training for horse started after man's first fall?

definitions.meaning: schooling a horse in precise movements
a whimsical ..., the era of clothing, began after Adam's Fall

explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Adam and Eve covered themselves only after the Fall, so the era of dress began then; 'first fall' tempts one to think of a rider tumbling off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the art of training a horse in obedience and deportment; the joke splits it into dress and age.

clue.text: Clothing for middle of wetter spell

parts.note: the two middle letters of wetter are a pair of Ts, which spelt in words says the answer

explanation.surface: Garments worn in the midst of a rainy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'wetter' is TT, which is said as 'double T'; 'spell' asks for that in words.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting man's jacket of the Renaissance, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Set standard of intelligence in this, for example.

indicators.note: in means the measure of intelligence is placed within the other word

parts.note: the clue you are reading is an example of a clue
IQ, intelligence quotient, is a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Set an intelligence benchmark in this puzzle, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' refers to the clue itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique is an exclusive set or group of people.

clue.text: Buddy often seen doing the Charleston

definitions.meaning: a sideways kick is a characteristic step in the 1920s Charleston dance

explanation.definitionFit: A sidekick is a companion; read as side kick it is a dance step.

clue.text: A venue for match away from home

parts.note: a field is where a match is played

explanation.surface: A ground for a game played on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means at a distance, far off.

clue.text: Pointed article about setback in educational circles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ca, from circa, means about

indicators.note: setback means the word for pointed is set backwards

parts.note: aimed means pointed, as a gun

explanation.surface: A barbed piece on a reverse in academic circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns AIMED into DEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Truth is, leader of Tories is this

definitions.text: Truth is, leader of Tories is this

parts.note: right means truth, what is correct

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word Tories

explanation.surface: The Conservative chief embodies conservatism, truthfully.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: the leader of the Tories is a right-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A rightist holds right-wing political views, like the Conservative leader.

clue.text: In queer street, money long since gone

indicators.note: queer means odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In financial trouble, the money having run out long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Being in queer street is British slang for being in debt. A tester was an old sixpence, long out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: A tester was a Tudor coin later used for a sixpence, obsolete currency.
